notes: acceptable_verdicts is a list, not a single value: any verdict in it counts as correct for this topic_id. evaluate_verdicts.py still records the exact verdict produced for the confusion matrix -- this list only controls what counts as correct.

A null acceptable_verdicts marks a topic this file does not score for verdict accuracy: sdvosb_setaside_eligibility, security_sanctions_representations, submission_deadline, contractor_certification_qualifications, and contractor_experience_tenure, since all five are is_text_verifiable: false in true_requirements.json and never get a verdict from a correctly-behaving pipeline.

The application deliberately varies its error types: compliant (7 topics), non_compliant (a quantity shortfall -- 2 past-performance contracts instead of 3), insufficient_information (a generic prior-experience statement missing the required per-year detail; an ambiguous, partially-triggered subcontractor-experience condition), and one contradictory claim (training certifications stated as both enclosed with the proposal and available only upon request).
description is copied verbatim from the matching topic_id in true_requirements.json so this file can be read alone; true_requirements.json is the source of truth if the two diverge.

prior_experience_documentation broadened to also accept non_compliant: the source solicitation text literally reads 'as the Prime Contractor Waste Removal Services' (an apparent leftover template artifact in an electrical-testing solicitation), and the model's non_compliant verdict (bidder shows electrical testing experience, not waste removal) is a defensible literal reading of that text, alongside the insufficient_information reading based on the intended/contextual meaning (missing per-year contract-detail breakdown).

verdicts.description: To be eligible for award of this SDVOSB set-aside, the offeror must be a small business under the assigned NAICS code and a certified SDVOSB listed in the SBA certification database; by submitting an offer the offeror represents it is an eligible, certified SDVOSB.
verdicts.rationale: is_text_verifiable: false in true_requirements.json -- actual SDVOSB certification/database status cannot be confirmed by reading the quote, only by checking the SBA certification database directly.

verdicts.description: By submitting its offer the offeror makes several standing legal representations/certifications triggered automatically by submission, including that it has conducted a reasonable inquiry and does not propose to use products/sources prohibited by an applicable FASCSA order, and that it does not conduct restricted business operations in Sudan.
verdicts.rationale: is_text_verifiable: false in true_requirements.json -- these are standing legal representations triggered automatically by submitting an offer, not something the offeror drafts content around.

verdicts.description: If subcontractors will be used, the offer must include at least two examples of the subcontractors' technical experience with similar contracts, in the same format as the offeror's own technical experience examples.
verdicts.rationale: Application mentions a subcontractor performed part of the work in one technical experience example, suggesting the conditional requirement may be triggered, but never provides the subcontractor's own technical experience examples in the required format.

verdicts.description: Offer must include electrical safety training certifications (OSHA 29 CFR 1910 Subpart S and NFPA 70E) submitted with the proposal, or, if unavailable, a written employer certification of having met this requirement submitted with the proposal.
verdicts.rationale: The Electrical Safety Training section first states that current training certifications 'are enclosed with this proposal,' then immediately states that certification records 'are available upon request rather than included in this proposal package' -- a direct contradiction about whether the certifications were actually submitted.

verdicts.description: Contractor must be currently certified as a NETA Certified Technician or via NICET, and have completed OSHA's approved 10-hour construction safety training.
verdicts.rationale: is_text_verifiable: false in true_requirements.json -- actual NETA/NICET certification and OSHA-10 completion status cannot be confirmed by reading the quote alone.

verdicts.description: Contractor must have technical training and a minimum of five continuous years of work experience in maintenance, inspection, and testing of low and medium voltage electrical power distribution systems in healthcare, industrial, educational, and commercial facilities.
verdicts.rationale: is_text_verifiable: false in true_requirements.json -- actual years of technical training and work-experience tenure is a background fact, not something the tender instructs the offeror to write into the quote.
